findings.title: Concurrent mobile logout and in-flight refresh/profile hydration can resurrect old tokens or overwrite the newly signed-in account.
findings.scenario: Sara opens Expo and an expired access token triggers refresh or /users/me. Sara signs out or switches to Tom before the request finishes. The older success callback unconditionally calls writeStoredSession/setUser, or a late refresh writes Sara's tokens after clearStoredSession. The old identity becomes active on the device even though the user intentionally left it.
findings.test_needed: Defer initial /me success and refresh response; logout or log in as another user before resolving each. Assert no old /me user or refresh token persisted, no old API Authorization and role home remains intended. Repeat native and Expo-web cases, including refresh failures and storage/network exceptions.

owner_question.question: When Sara logs out while an earlier refresh/profile request is pending, may the app silently restore Sara's saved account or overwrite Tom's subsequent login?
options: No; invalidate all in-flight auth writes on identity change and logout
Only if the earlier HTTP call was already sent before logout
Yes; accept current asynchronous restoration behavior

findings.title: Signing out of Expo leaves its push token registered to the prior account, so private alerts can keep arriving on a signed-out device.
findings.scenario: Sara signs out from a shared iPhone. Native logout clears local secure tokens but never deletes/deactivates that device's push registration. The backend logout only blacklists the refresh token. Notifications notify_users still looks up every active DeviceToken for Sara and delivers future alert titles/bodies to the same phone.
findings.test_needed: Register an Expo push token while Sara is logged in. Sign out through native app. Trigger a new private message/notification for Sara; assert DeviceToken is inactive or removed and no push sent. Log in as Tom and confirm token belongs only to Tom. Server logout should revoke current device independently of client network reliability.

owner_question.question: Should Sara's private shift, employment and chat alerts continue displaying on a phone after she signs out?
options: No; revoke the current device's push token on logout server-side
Only send generic notifications without personal details until next login
Yes; preserve notifications after signing out
